Then, the vehicle arrival rate function is used to construct an objective function, i.e., the problem of minimizing system transmission the overall latency. we propose the hybrid V2V/V2I transmission method that determines the communication transmission mode of the vehicles to minimize transmission latency. The simulation results show that the overall transmission latency is substantially lower for the hybrid V2V/V2I transmission method than the pure V2I transmission method with the transmission packet size and vehicle speed varying.

articleTitle: RIS-aided Wireless Power Transfer for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach of wireless power transfer for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with the assistance of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). The optimal energy beamforming at the power station, passive phase adjustment at the RIS, and the harvested energy of the UAVs are discussed. Then, the wireless power transfer efficiency of a two-UAV case is investigated, as well as the optimal position of the RIS. In addition, the minimum RIS scale that guarantees a power transfer efficiency gain over the traditional system without RIS is analyzed. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified by simulation results. It is shown that the RIS has potential advantages in improving the PTE comparing with the traditional system without RIS, but a certain requirement on the RIS scale.

articleTitle: Gated Bi-Recurrent Separate Network for Video Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Video super-resolution (VSR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) video sequences from low-resolution (LR) video sequences by image processing, which has been widely applied to different scenarios, including ultra HD video display, object detection, and medical image reconstruction. VSR exploits both intra-frame information and inter-frame information and makes full use of spatial and temporal information to reconstruct images, thus outperforming single-image super-resolution (SISR). In this paper, a gated bi-recurrent separate network (GBSN) is proposed, which gets spatio-temporal information to ensure a fine and realistic reconstruction of each frame by utilizing the bi-recurrent coupled propagation structure. The gated structure is used to control feature updating, which limits the propagation of error features. For the bidirectional network, the low-frequency part of the image is reconstructed in forward and the corresponding high-frequency part is reconstructed in backward. A fusion module is further developed to integrate these two parts. Experiments have been conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method, where Vid4, UDM10, and Vimeo-90K-T datasets are adopted. As compared to the state-of-the-art VSR methods in the literature, the proposed method enhances the peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR) to 28.51dB on Vid4 and 39.84dB on UDM10, respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-Edge Computing Offloading for Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Recently, the Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) has been a hotspot and difficulty in the fifth-generation (5G) communication. With the ever-increasing demands on the accuracy and immediacy of data, the size of computing tasks is growing rapidly, which will exceed the rate of data processing in local devices. To tackle this problem, the Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) systems can provide a flexible and efficient approach to offload the learning tasks from capacity-limited local devices to its connected computation-intensive edge nodes. To provide satisfactory Quality of Service (QoS) for the URLLC tasks, it is significant to investigate task offloading schemes. However, lots of related works focus on the offloading schemes in single edge node cases. To further improve the computing efficiency, we propose a novel framework to jointly optimize the task offloading among multiple edge nodes in this work. Specifically, we at first propose a task division rule based on minimum granularity decomposition. Secondly, we formulate a task offloading optimization problem to minimize the total delay with limited resources, in which both the task queue status in edge nodes and the transmission circumstances are considered. To solve the NP-hard problem efficiently, we prove that the original problem can be transformed into an equivalent mixed integer programming one, and then introduce the Branch and Bound (B & B) algorithm to obtain a global optimal solution. Finally, we provide the simulation results to evaluate our model. The results show that the B & B algorithm outperforms the greedy, average and random algorithms, especially for the cases with computation-intensive tasks, limited number of available edge nodes and unevenly distributed of edge nodes' computation resources.

articleTitle: Reflection Coefficients Optimization in IRS-assisted Communication: An Evolutionary Game Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) alters the signal propagation via tuning a large number of passive reflection units, and is a promising solution to enhance the wireless communication. In this paper, we aim to improve the level of mutual information of the IRS-assisted communication system by optimizing the IRS reflection coefficients. Specifically, in order to solve the established IRS reflection coefficients optimization problem, the dynamic adjustment process is first modeled as an evolutionary game (EG) model, and then the replication dynamic equations about the revenue function are established. Next, for the single-mode constraints of the reflection coefficients, the reinforcement learning (RL) method is adopted, and the strategy iteration algorithm is used to solve the evolutionary stability strategy. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed algorithm achieves substantially increased mutual information compared to the traditional scheme without IRS and another benchmark scheme.

articleTitle: Peak AoI vs. Delay: Closed-Form Analysis in the Finite Block Length Regime
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Both age of information (AoI) and delay are critical performance metrics of emerging time-sensitive applications. However, their inherent relationship in the finite block length (FBL) regime has remained open as it is affected by block length and update rate in a complex manner. In this paper, we derive closed-form expressions and their tight approximations for the average peak AoI (PAoI) (upper bound on AoI) and the average delay for an FBL Last-Come First-Served system with the retransmission and non-preemption policy, based on which we present a comprehensive analysis of the relationship between the two performance metrics in the FBL regime. It is proved that there exists a strong tradeoff between the average delay and the average PAoI, given a block length, and that the average delay is mono-increasing with respect to the average PAoI, given an update rate. In particular, the average delay is derived as a closed-form function of the average PAoI, and its infimum value is shown to be half of that of the average PAoI, as verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Optimized Construction of Short and High Rate Protograph QC-LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To obtain efficient and pragmatic channel codes high signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), an optimized construction of short and high rate protograph quasi-cyclic (QC) low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes is presented. Based on an optimized protograph template, the code framework is firstly produced by the extensions of the variable nodes. By enlarging the dimension of the sub-matrices related to the protograph framework, the base quasi-cyclic (QC) matrix is generated with required code rate and length. Then, the elements in the base matrix are split with even smaller square sub-matrices of the same row and column weights. In this procedure, a progressive edge growth (PEG) algorithm is employed to find the optimized positions of the QC submatrices, which brings larger girth for better code performance. Also the circulant offsets in all QC sub-matrices are optimally searched by a QC improved approximated cycle extrinsic message degree (QCI-ACE) algorithm, which improves the relationship of the unavoidable loops in the code's Tanner graph and thus it improves the error floor. Simulation results show that the codes produced by the proposed method demonstrate quite good bit error rate (BER) performance. In addition, they exhibit good properties of high spectrum efficiency by the high code rate, as well as the low complexity by the short code length. Therefore, the proposed code construction can be efficiently applied in the design of short and high rate protograph QC-LDPC codes with high rate and rational complexity.

articleTitle: The maximal coin-walker entanglement in quantum walks with ballistic transports
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: We experimentally show the first realization of the maximal entanglement under a ballistic quantum transport. An inhomogeneous ordered quantum walk is introduced to generate the maximal entanglement meanwhile maintaining the quadratic speedup, wherein the coin operations keep unchanged with time evolution but are varied according to positions in a deterministic way. Using a reconfigurable time-bin encoded optical network, we implement a 11-step ballistic quantum walk and obtain a maximal entanglement in which the von Neumann entropy of the coin state is close to 1. The construction of the maximal entanglement and the speedup of spreading signify a quadratic acceleration in producing entanglement with fast expansion of the Hilbert space, thus may stimulate the engineering of entanglement and the design of quantum algorithms.

articleTitle: Left Ventricle Segmentation based on a Segmentation-Adversarial Network with Complementary Labels
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Accurate segmentation of the endocardium and epicardium of the left ventricle in some cardiac images, such as tMRIs, is a facet of clinical quantitative analysis. The complex structure of the cardiac system makes accurate heart segmentation a challenging task. Generative adversarial networks offer great advantages in learning data modeling, and adversarial training can effectively promote network parameters updatings. Segmentation-adversarial networks are a new popular means for segment image objects. However, this model requires abundant segmentation labels to complete model training, and it is difficult to achieve good medical image segmentation results. This paper proposes that complementary labels can be used to double the feature channels in the segmenting-adversarial network. In this way, more features can be supplied from the current training set, which can improve the training performance of the segmentation-adversarial network. In addition, the approach can reduce the impact of insufficient training data on model training. Additionally, the application of group normalization was found to further improve left ventricle segmentation accuracy. The validity of the proposed approach is illustrated through experiments.

articleTitle: Optimal Transmission Strategy for Solar Harvesting Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: We consider a solar harvesting point-to-point communication system, where the transmitter powered by solar energy and equipped with a battery of finite capacity communicates over an AWGN channel. The solar harvesting rate is described by the real data-based quadratic solar power model, which characterizes the solar power levels by a quadratic equation with the time of the day. By analyzing the effect of battery capacity, we consider two cases and propose an optimal transmission strategy for each case to maximize the channel capacity. Furthermore, we prove the optimality of the proposed strategy through the proof by contradiction. We find that for a certain amount of energy, longer transmission time and more uniform energy allocation for transmission lead to greater capacity.

articleTitle: Achievable Rate Analysis for Distributed Intelligent Reflecting Surface-Aided MIMO Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate an distributed intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication system. To maximize the achievable rate of the receiver under the transmit power constraint of the transmitter, we jointly optimize the active beamforming at the transmitter and passive beamforming at the IRSs, respectively. Since the problem is non-convex, we propose an alternating optimization algorithm by iteratively optimizing the transmit precoding matrix or one of the reflection coefficients with the others being fixed. Simulation results show that our proposed scheme can achieve higher achievable rate compared with other benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: L-VDA: A Lightweight Deep Learning Algorithm for Vehicle Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: As the key technology of Advanced Driving Assistance System (ADAS), Forward Collision Warning (FCW) enables drivers to perceive the danger in advance through targeted warning at a reasonable time, so as to reduce or avoid the occurrence of collision accidents. However, the high computational complexity of the existing FCW system seriously affects real-time vehicle detection and further leads to traffic safety hazards. In lieu of this, this paper proposes a lightweight vehicle detection algorithm i.e., L-VDA, which uses deep separable convolution to minimize the total number of parameters required to train the model while ensuring detection accuracy. Specifically, this paper firstly proposes a lightweight backbone network i.e., My-MobileNet for multi-scale feature extraction. Then, Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP) and Path Aggregation Network (PANet) are used for further feature fusion. Moreover, the priori box is obtained by clustering method and Non-maximum Suppression (NMS) algorithm to get more accurate vehicle detection results. Finally, by training on a variety of data sets such as KITTI data set, UA-DETRAC data set and the data set collected in Xi'an, the robustness of the detection algorithm is optimized. Moreover, experiment results indicate that the proposed L-VDA can achieve low computation complexity while ensuring detection accuracy compared with existing strategies such as YOLOv4 and YOLOv4+MobileNet. Especially, when L-VDA is used to detect the KITTI data set, the weight of the model is only 26.8M, which was reduced by nine times compared with YOLOv4, and the average precision reaches 95.2%.

articleTitle: Robust Localization Based on RSS and TDOA Combination in Complex Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In order to meet the requirement of the source localization under the environment of the non-line-of-sight transmission for the wireless signal, the combination method of the received signal strength and the time difference of arrival is proposed. By introducing the balancing parameters, the original non-convex problem of the maximum likelihood estimator is converted into a generalized trust region subproblem. Then, the rough estimation of the target's position is obtained based on the bisection procedure. The iterative algorithm is adopted to refine the result and guarantee the robustness. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Location-assisted Beam Tracking and Selection for Downlink MISO via Unsupervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: For the millimeter wave mobile communication systems, the existing beam alignment schemes frequently perform beam training and adjust beam direction to select the best beam during the movement of the mobile terminal, which is costly in terms of hardware implementation and signal processing complexity. In this paper, we exploit the spatial consistency feature of the channels at the adjacent locations to improve the total achievable rate while reducing the frequency of beam adjustment. To this end, we design the beam selection matrix with the target of maximizing the sum of the total achievable rate per the frequency of beam adjustment at the transmitter. The formulated problem is a non-convex integer programming problem and is difficult to be solved. To address the non-convex and non-linear optimization problem, we propose a convolutional neural network (CNN) structure-based heuristic algorithm to optimize the beam selection matrix via the predicted channel characteristics. Numerical results show that the performance of the proposed scheme is better than that of the maximum-achievable-rate scheme, even when the trajectory prediction error reaches 0.25.

articleTitle: Joint Channel, Power and Bandwidth Optimization for Anti-jamming Communications: A Multi-agent Q-learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To facilitate external malicious jamming and interference in multi-user anti-jamming communication networks, in this paper, a novel joint channel, power and bandwidth optimization model is constructed. Channel reconstruction technology and sleep mechanism are introduced to avoid channel access conflict and jamming. Besides, joint probability distribution is adopted to characterize incomplete channel state information (CSI) caused by complex electromagnetic environment. Based on the system model, a multi-agent Q-learning approach based on joint optimization anti-jamming is adopted. Simulations show that the proposed algorithm can achieve better communication utility and maximum communication transmission rate of the whole network than the comparison algorithms.

articleTitle: Waveform Shaping for PAPR Reduction in OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the waveform shaping for peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. Unlike the previous literature, we take both the PAPR of the transmitted signal and the error vector magnitude (EVM) of the received signal into account and constrain the average power of the transmitted signal. For this purpose, we formulate an optimization problem that jointly minimizes the PAPR and EVM under constant average power constraint. Due to the non-convexity of the power constraint, the optimization problem is difficult to solve. To end this, an iterative algorithm is proposed to solve the joint optimization problem. Furthermore, to improve the capability of the algorithm for a large number of subcarriers, we develop another efficient optimization algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed algorithms can achieve near optimal PAPR performance with superior EVM performance.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Learning Approach for UAVs Enabled Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology provides a potential solution to scalable wireless edge networks. This paper uses two UAVs, with accelerated motions and fixed altitudes, to realize a wireless edge network, where one UAV forwards the downlink signal to user terminals (UTs) distributed over an area where another UAV collects uplink data. Both downlink and uplink transmissions consider the active user probability and the queue structure as well as the hovering times of UAVs. Specifically, we develop a novel joint Q-Learning multi-agent (JQ-LMA) algorithm to maximize the overall energy efficiency of the edge networks, through optimizing the UAVs trajectories, transmit powers, and the resistant distance between UAVs. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves much higher energy efficiency than other benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: Contract-Based Resource Allocation Approach in Cooperative Parked Vehicular Computing Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a contract-based resource allocation approach in cooperative parked vehicular edge computing (PVEC) networks. We firstly consider a novel PVEC architecture in which parked vehicles (PV s) are coupled with dedicated VEC servers for the cooperative provision of computing resources. Each type of PV s and its corresponding VEC servers are regarded as a PV- VEC unit. Secondly, the utilities of the service provider (SP) and PV- VEC units are formulated and a contract-based resource allocation problem is designed for the maximization of SP's utility. Considering that it is intractable to solve the optimization problem directly, the primal problem is simplified by incentive mechanism and decoupled into two subproblems. For optimal contract design, we solve the subproblems by Lagrangian multiplier method and dual function. Simulation results demonstrate the validity of each optimal contract for its corresponding type and the superiority of proposed PVC with optimal contract design over other existing works in improving resource scheduling when the overall energy cost of SP is considered.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation for IRS-Assisted Multi-User Millimeter Wave MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is a promising technology for future wireless communication. To fully utilize the advantages of the IRS, the acquisition of accurate channel state information (CSI) is necessary. In this paper, we propose a manifold optimization-based channel estimation (MO-CE) algorithm for an IRS-assisted millimeter wave (mmWave) MIMO system with multiple users. In particular, by exploiting the sparsity of channel matrices and applying the Least Squares (LS) criterion, we formulate a multiple coupled complex fixed-rank (CFR) matrices optimization problem for channel estimation in the multiple users scenario. The problem is then transformed to several subproblems to reduce problem size and decouple multiple matrix variables. Furthermore, the CFR Hermitian positive semidefinite (PSD) manifold helps to satisfy CFR constraint by using semidefinite lifting. A Riemannian conjugate gradient-based movement is performed separately on the manifold, and the convergence of the proposed algorithm is established over the manifold too. Simulation results are provided to show the superiority of the proposed MO-CE algorithm in comparison with two benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: Cognitive Radio Primary Network Secure Communication Strategy Based on Energy Harvesting and Destination Assistance
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Cognitive radio primary network secure communication strategy based on secondary user energy harvesting and primary user destination assistance is investigated to guarantee primary user secure communication in cognitive radio network. In the proposed strategy, the primary network selects the best secondary user to forward the traffic from a primary transmitter (PT) to a primary receiver (PR). The best secondary user implements beamforming technique to assist primary network for secure communication. The remaining secondary transmitters harvest energy and transmit information to secondary receiver over the licensed primary spectrum. In order to further enhance the security of primary network and increase the harvested energy for the remaining secondary users, a destination-assisted jamming signal transmission strategy is proposed. In this strategy, artificial noise jamming signal transmitted by PR not only confuses eavesdropper, but also be used to power the remaining secondary users. Simulation results demonstrate that, the proposed strategy allows secondary users to communicate in the licensed primary spectrum. It enhances primary network secure communication performance dramatically with the joint design of secondary user transmission power and beamforming vectors. Furthermore, physical layer security of primary and secondary network can also be guaranteed via the proposed cognitive radio primary network secure communication strategy.

articleTitle: Precoding Design for IRS-Assisted Full-Duplex Self-Backhauled Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Full-duplex self-backhauling that the backhaul link and the access link utilize the same spectrum has higher downlink rate compared to conventional self-backhauled network, while the cross-tier interference by spectrum sharing becomes a new challenge. Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is a promising alternative to solve the problem. This paper studies a full-duplex self-backhauled system assisted with IRS, in which the problem is formulated as a user rate maximization problem. We propose an alternating optimization algorithm and a two-stage algorithm to jointly optimize the beamforming weight vectors of the base stations (BSs) and the phase shift vector of IRS. The simulation results show the performance of these two optimization algorithms and verify the improvement assisted with IRS in different setups.

articleTitle: Predicting the size of the pre-expanded balloon for coronary denove lesion by deep learning
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The selection of the medical instruments size is the key to the success of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). At present, the selection of the medical instrument size mainly depends on the subjective judgment and experience of doctors, which will increase the risk and reduce the efficiency of the operation process. Inspired by the application of the deep learning technology in improving the clinical treatment effect, stenosis segmentation and vascular disease detection, we are committed to verifying whether the deep learning method can predict the size of the pre-expanded balloon for coronary denove lesion, so as to provide a reference size for doctors during the operation. In order to achieve this goal, we build a densnet neural network model with the squeeze and exclusion block (SE block) to verify the prediction effect of the medical instrument size. The data set used in the experiment is collected and standardized by ourselves. We use 100 X-ray coronary angiography images as the training set, 10 images as the validation set, and 10 images as the test set. The experimental results show that there is a high correlation between the predicted value of the deep learning model and the true value manually labeled. Even in the case of small amount of data, the predicted result of the model is still close to the true value, so the deep learning method can be applied to the prediction of the medical instruments size.

articleTitle: Location-Aided Deep Learning-Based Channel Estimation for Hybrid Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In hybrid analog-digital (HAD) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, channel estimation is a critical challenge due to information loss caused by limited radio-frequency chains. The conventional compressive sensing (CS) algorithms suffer from unsatisfactory performance and high complexity. In this paper, we propose a novel location-aided deep learning (DL)-based framework to better exploit the sparsity structure of channels in the angular domain. Specifically, the entire angular space is segmented into many small regions and a dedicated neural network is trained offline for each region. During testing, the most suitable network is selected based on the location information of the user. Inside each network, the region-specific measurement matrix and channel estimator are jointly optimized, which not only improves the signal measurement efficiency, but also enhances the channel estimation capability. Simulation results show that the proposed approach significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art CS algorithm and the conventional measurement matrix.

articleTitle: A 3D Non-Stationary GBSM for Underwater Acoustic MIMO Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: A three dimensional (3D) geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM) for underwater acoustic (UWA) wireless communication systems in shallow sea is proposed in this paper. Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) sonar setting is supported in this model and some characteristics such as the wideband property, multipath propagation, and non-stationarity of UWA channels are taken into account. The time autocorrelation function (ACF) and spatial cross-correlation function (CCF) of UWA communication channels are derived and simulated. The simulation results show that this model can describe the characteristics of UWA channels accurately.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Resource Allocation for NOMA-Based Broadcasting Vehicular Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) has been considered a promising technology to further reduce latency and increase reliability in vehicular networks. Recently, most relevant studies have focused on maximizing the overall performance of NOMA-based vehicular networks, such as the total throughput or the average package receptive ratio. Different from existing works, our study investigates the optimal clustering and resource allocation in vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communications that underlie a NOMA-based vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) network. Our objective is to maximize the time-based proportional fairness for the V2V users while guaranteeing the quality of service for the embedded V2I users. Particularly, the position-based optimal clustering for V2V transmitters is derived first, and then subchannel assignment is obtained given the optimal clusters. Finally, a multi-agent distributed power control algorithm is performed to solve the problem efficiently. The simulation results validate that the proposed resource allocation algorithms outperform the reference algorithms.

articleTitle: Uplink Ergodic Capacity of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Aided Multi-User MISO Communications With Statistical CSI
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is a promising solution to build a programmable wireless environment with reconfigurable passive elements, which can achieve high spectral and energy efficiency. In this paper, we investigate the ergodic capacity of RIS-assisted multi-user multiple-input single-output (MISO) wireless systems in uplink scenario. Unlike most of prior works, where instantaneous channel state information (CSI) is assumed, we consider the realistic scenario with only statistical CSI. Specifically, we first present an analytical expressions for the ergodic sum capacity of the system. Based on which, the joint power control and phase shift design problem maximizing the ergodic sum capacity is formulated. Simulation results are presented to validate the accuracy of the analytical ergodic sum capacity expressions and evaluate the impact of key system parameters such as CSI and Rician <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> factor. The findings suggest that the proposed statistical CSI design achieves decent performance compared with the instantaneous CSI based design.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Routing in Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: 6G-Wisdom Connected Everything has been put into research and development. It breaks through the limitations of topography and surface and extends to natural spaces such as space, air, land, and ocean. Whether it is national defense missions, emergency communications, or large-scale deterministic services, the integration of space, air and ground has significant advantages. This paper mainly focuses on the research of the space-air-ground integrated network. The new network architecture is bound to face new problems, among which routing is the basis of network interconnection. Currently, existing routing schemes are generally aimed at single-layer network routing, and cooperative routing between multiple layers has not made much progress. Due to the diversity of node types in the network, the limitations of different layers are also different. For example, satellite bandwidth resources are limited, time delay is large, hot air balloon energy is limited, and the ground is easily affected by the geographical environment. Aiming at the above problems, this paper proposes an integrated space-air-ground routing scheme based on reinforcement learning. Through the design of reinforcement learning and its reward function, we take the lowest delay as the goal, and the remaining energy and bandwidth utilization as the constraint conditions for routing. Theoretical analysis and simulation results show that reinforcement learning effectively solves the problem of limited satellite bandwidth resources and hot air balloons energy in the space-air-ground integrated network, and can successfully implement the routing function. Compared with Floyd routing, latency, packet loss rate and bandwidth utilization performance have all significantly improved.

articleTitle: Mobility and Traffic Prediction-Based Resource Allocation With Edge Intelligence in Wireless Network
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Radio resources are increasingly scarce with the explosive growth of smart end devices while these resources are under-utilized in existing wireless networks. Deep learning can make full use of wireless big data to predict information from both the user and network side. Thus, predictive resource allocation applying intelligence learning at network edge is a promising approach to improve the system performance. In this paper, we formulate a prediction-based resource allocation policy (PBRA) with edge intelligence in a large time scale aiming to improve system throughput. A proportion factor is proposed to adapt to channel gains, user mobility and quality-of-service (QoS) with predictive information, which can be predicted by edge intelligence server deployed at network edge. Then, we propose the PBRA algorithm in a small time scale with solved optimal policy in the large time scale. Simulation results show that the proposed PBRA policy achieves higher throughput and improves QoS even compared with fair proportion scheduling policy with error-free predictive information.

articleTitle: Impacts of Angles-of-Arrival on the Performance of Space-Constrained MIMO Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With an infinite number of antennas deployed in the space-constrained environment, limits of the measures for the uplink multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) diversity system, i.e., the conditional long-term signal-power-to-interference-power ratio (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SIRP}_{c}$</tex>) and the conditional long-term signal amplitude to the square root of the interference power ratio (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SAPR}_{c}$</tex>) given the angles-of-arrival (AOAs) of the line-of-sight (LOS) signal components, are derived for users in correlated Ricean fading channels. The impacts of the user AOAs on these measures are discussed. Furthermore, the asymptotic user achievable spectral efficiency and bit error rate are derived using the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SIRP}_{c}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SARP}_{c}$</tex>, respectively, which indicates these performance indices vary with the AOAs of the user signals. We point out the LOS components, which dramatically change the system measure and performance with different AOAs, are sometimes beneficial. Results show by avoiding picking users located in the same direction of the antenna array, the correlated Ricean fading scenario can achieve superior performance to that of the correlated Rayleigh fading scenario.

articleTitle: A Novel Sparse Reconstruction Based DOA Estimation Method Under Grid Mismatch
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Under the condition of gain-phase errors, the existing methods only consider that the arrival angle strictly falls on the divided grid, which will pose limitation on the accuracy of the direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. In this paper, a new DOA estimation method based on sparse reconstruction is proposed, which applies the first-order Taylor expansion to modify the array output model under the condition of grid mismatch, and then uses the alternate optimization method to solve the non-convex optimization problem, obtaining the grid angle and bias angle. Compared with the existing methods, the proposed method improves the accuracy of the DOA estimation without requiring change of the grid spacing. This method also performs independent of array phase errors. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Joint Placement and Scheduling Optimization for Wireless Content Caching Networks: An I/O Latency Minimization Consideration
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, a joint content packets placement and scheduling optimization problem is investigated to minimize the in put/output (I/O) latency of wireless content caching networks (WCCNs), taking into account the real content coding mode, namely, repetition coding, and successful retrieving criterion in practical systems. The formulated non-convex integer programming problem is optimally solved by a one-dimension search-based algorithm with feasibility checking through equivalent problem transformation. We also analyze the time complexity of the designed solution. Extensive numerical simulation results reveal that the proposed joint optimization algorithm outperforms the baseline scheme significantly in terms of I/O latency as well as outage performance.

articleTitle: Social Awareness-Based Collaboration Interferes With Physical Layer Secure Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper proposes a social-aware cooperative interference strategy for physical layer security, which not only considers the physical characteristics of the devices, but also considers the social relationship among users, and combines the two to increase the confidentiality capacity of the communication network. This paper studies the security issue of a multi-user communication network in the existence of eavesdropper and the source node with the help of cooperative interference node. To be specific, we define a trust value for each node to indicate the social relations and network interactivity between nodes. This paper proposes a two-layer network cooperative interference system model, by constructing the utility function of the main channel and the utility function of the eavesdropping channel, and the goal of maximizing the utility function of the entire network is proposed. The problem can be described as a one-to-one matching game, and the simulation results display that this scheme can obtain a higher confidentiality rate compared with the existing scheme.

articleTitle: A Cascaded Adaboost-BP Diabetes Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the rapid increase in the prevalence and incidence of diabetes, it has posed severe challenges to global public health. Early diagnosis, early treatment, and early prediction of diabetes are important measures to alleviate this trend. Current machine learning models cannot effectively process data features in the prediction of diabetes, which will affect the prediction results to a certain extent. Aiming at this problem, this paper proposes an integrated model based on BP neural network and AdaBoost boosting tree to achieve accurate prediction of diabetes. The model first trains the AdaBoost base classifier and the BP neural network base classifier separately, and then trains the weight parameters of the base classifier through the weighted neural network to form a strong classifier ensemble model to complete the diabetes prediction task. The experimental results show that the prediction accuracy reaches 91.23%, which is 3.19% higher than other advanced models, which greatly improves the accuracy of diabetes prediction.

articleTitle: Average Peak Age of Information in the Cognitive IoT Systems with Prediction
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper is motivated by the high information freshness requirement of some status update applications in the cognitive Internet of Things (IoT). The recently proposed metric, age of information (AoI), is adopted to characterize the status update performance. We propose a novel prediction based status update scheme to improve the status update performance for unauthorized users in the cognitive IoT. Due to the limited spectrum resources, a machine type communication (MTC) device, as the unauthorized user, reuses the channel of the primary user under overlay mode, and sends status packets to a central controller (CC). We analyze the prediction and decoding performance for the MTC, and derive the closed-form expression of the average peak AoI at the CC. Simulation and numerical results verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis, and show that the proposed prediction based status update method outperforms the traditional status update methods without prediction.

articleTitle: 5G Multi-Service-Oriented User Association and Routing Algorithm for Integrated Terrestrial-Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we study the data transmission problem in an uplink scenario of an integrated terrestrial-satellite network (ITSN) which consists of a 5G next generation node-B (gNB), a number of satellites, a satellite gateway (GW), a number of enhanced mobile broadband users (EUs) and massive machine type communication users (MUs). We assume that EUs and MUs need to send their data to the core network through gNB association mode (gNB-AM) or satellite association mode (SAM). On account of various characteristics of EUs and MUs, we first determine gNB-AM for the two types of users, and then propose a deferred acceptance (DA) algorithm-based clustering strategy for MUs. Based on the obtained user association and clustering strategy, we formulate route selection problem of EUs in SAM as a constrained energy consumption optimization problem. To solve the formulated problem, we transform the problem into two subproblems, i.e., inter-satellite routing subproblem and user association subproblem, and solve the two subproblems based on Q-learning algorithm and Kuhn-Munkres (K-M) algorithm, respectively. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Flexible Duplexing Mode Selection Optimization for Network-Assisted Full-Duplex Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Network-assisted full-duplex enables simultaneous uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) communications by allocating remote antenna units (RAUs) to perform either UL reception of DL transmission at each time slot, which improve the spectral efficiency (SE) of cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. However, the previous studies usually fix the duplex mode of RAUs to analyze the system performance. A more flexible duplex technology concerning mode selection of RAUs is introduced to solve the resource allocation problem of CF MIMO systems. RAUs can flexibly adapt UL or DL working mode to utilize the UL/DL resource efficiently. This letter proposed a duplex mode selection algorithm based on parallel successive convex approximation and mathematical transformation skills. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves a higher SE gain than other traditional schemes with lower complexity.

articleTitle: An Improved Support Vector Machine based Electric Power Grid Terminal Security Access
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved Support Vector Machine (SVM) based 5G wireless terminal security access method for electric power grid. Aiming at the problem of a lack of standard parameter selection in SVM algorithm, this paper proposes an improved Differential Evolution algorithm(DE) for the SVM. The minimum classification error rate is chosen as the optimization criterion, the optimized combinatorial parameters in SVM can be obtained by using the improved DE. The experimental results show that the authentication accuracy of the proposed method is higher than traditional methods.

articleTitle: A Random Multi-channel Spectral Graph Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have been widely used to process graph data. However, the ability of most traditional graph models to integrate node features and topology is not ideal. In this case, the Adaptive Multi-channel Graph Convolution Networks (AMGCN) model is proposed to redesign the model structure. It can greatly improve the fusion ability of topology and node features in complex graphs with rich information. Nevertheless, this model cannot solve the problems of over-smoothness and non-robustness as the depth of the model increases. To address this issue, we propose A Random Multi-channel Spectral Graph Convolution Network (RMSGCN). It adopts a random propagation strategy to reduce potential noise interference from high-order neighbors. Moreover, this model introduces simple spectral graph convolution (SSGC) to enhance the model's ability in deep convolution. A large number of experiments on five data sets show that our model has better performance. It has better expressive power in deep convolution.

articleTitle: Joint Transceiver and IRS Design in MIMO PS-SWIPT System
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) assisted multi-input multi-output (MIMO) simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) system with multiple power splitting receivers (PSRs). We aim at maximizing the weighted sum-rate (WSR) of the system through jointly designing the PS ratio of each PSR, the active transmit beamforming (ATB) of the access point (AP) and the passive reflective beamforming (PRB) of the IRS, while the constraints on the AP, PSRs and IRS are satisfied. However, since the variables are intricately coupled and the constraints are conflicting, the formulated problem is non-convex. We propose a framework to jointly design the AP, the PSRs and the IRS. Particularly, first we transform this problem into an equivalently form based on fractional programming methods. Then, we decompose the transformed problem into several subproblems, and more important, we exploit the successive convex approximation method to recast the non-convex constraints, so as to transform the subproblems as convex form and then solve them alternately. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm achieves a substantial improvement performance gain over baseline schemes.

articleTitle: Laser Charging for UAV-based FSO-RF Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this work, the outage performance of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based relaying system is investigated, where an UAV works as a relay to transmit the signal between the source and the destination. More specifically, we assume that an optical equipment with free-space optical (FSO) communication ability which is located at a high building is employed to provide laser charging. Then, the harvested energy is used as the power for the UAV. Based on this setting, an analytical formula of the outage probability is derived by exploiting the bivariate Fox-H function. Numerical results are carried out to validate our analysis.

articleTitle: Joint User Grouping and Resource Allocation for Multi-Beam Satellite System with Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To ensure the fairness of user service and the transmission rate of multi-beam satellite system with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), a joint optimization algorithm of user grouping and power allocation is proposed. We formulate a transmission rate maximization resource allocation problem in multi-beam satellite system under the constraints of the user grouping, the maximum transmit power of the satellite and the minimum quality of service (QoS) for users. In order to solve the non-convex problem, a clustering-based NOMA user grouping algorithm is proposed. Based on the grouping result, the original non-convex power allocation sub-problem is converted into a convex optimization problem by taylor approximation method. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieve better transmission rate performance compared with the existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Joint Transceiver and Passive Beamforming Optimization for RIS-Assisted MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates the transceiver and beamforming design for a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-antenna communication system. We aim to minimize the weighted mean-squared error of the received data by jointly optimizing the precoder, the passive RIS beamforming, and the receiving filter of the system, subject to a transmit power constraint and unit-modulus constraints imposed on the RIS reflection coefficients. In order to tackle the nonconvexity of this design problem, we propose a computationally-efficient algorithm based on alternating optimization, where the solutions to the precoder, the RIS beamforming, and the receiving filter are derived in semi-closed forms and closed-form, respectively. The convergence of the proposed algorithm is theoretically proved. Numerical results validate the performance superiority of the proposed algorithm over various existing benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: A method for automatic detection of teacher's gaze area based on smart classroom system
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The quality of teaching is closely related to the ability of the teacher, which is still mostly assessed in the traditional way. With the development of artificial intelligence, smart classroom systems are beginning to appear, which can quantify and analyze the teaching data in the classroom to produce corresponding results for teaching management or teaching evaluation. Therefore, this paper proposes an automatic method for detecting the teacher's position and gaze area based on the smart classroom system. The method mainly uses adaptive area face detection technology, face feature point matching, head pose acquisition and teacher gaze point calculation algorithms to automatically obtain the teacher's position and gaze area distribution in the classroom. Through experiments and public classroom tests, it was found that the maximum mean error in teacher position obtained by this method was 11.72cm and that the teacher's area of gaze was largely consistent with the actual change. This method can also be used to assess teaching ability and quality, and the data obtained can also be used as a learning resource for novice teachers or average students, so that they can continuously improve their teaching ability.

articleTitle: A 3GPP-Based Height-Dependent LoS Probability Model for A2G Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, combing with the machine learning (ML) principle, a height-dependent line-of-sight (LoS) probability prediction method based on the 3GPP model is developed. We adopt the ray-tracing (RT) simulation method instead of field measurement to acquire channel data and develop the back propagation neural network (BPNN) to estimate height-dependent parameters. In order to introduce the factor of height to the LoS probability, we study the relationship between the parameters and aerial platforms height. The simulation results show that our proposed model can effectively predict the LoS probability for different heights. Moreover, the predicted results match the RT-based ones better than the original method recommended by the 3GPP model.

articleTitle: Spectrum Analysis of 2.4 GHz Band Based on Successive Signal Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The high cost of cellular spectrum has motivated network providers to extend LTE to unlicensed band. The 2.4 GHz band is an attractive choice since it provides higher penetration and coverage. However, operating in 2.4 GHz band inevitably suffers serious interference from heterogeneous network devices. We in this paper propose a 2.4 GHz band spectrum analysis method, which is the important first step to build reliable connections among LTE devices in the 2.4 GHz band. Our method involves two stages. It first locates and captures the interference signal on the time-frequency spectrogram with a region growing-based image segmentation method. With the extracted signal, it then identifies the type of interference technology based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). The obtained information (i.e., the type and the time-frequency position of the interference on the spectrogram) provided the base for the interference avoidance and resistance methods. Experimental evaluation shows that the proposed spectrum analysis system can locate low-power (1.09 dB) signal with high accuracy and achieves a classification accuracy of 96.15%.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Microwave Sampler Based on Step Recovery Diode
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: A new type of broadband microwave sampler is designed in this paper. It can work in 20–50 GHz. The circuit of microwave sampler has the following three parts, including the balun, pulse generator circuit and sampling diode circuit. In the pulse generator circuit, we only use the step recovery diode (SRD) to generate very narrow sampling pulse. Compared with the short circuit microstrip line pulse generator, it can generate higher sampling level. As a result, sampling diodes can be started more easily. This microwave sampler also has good conversion loss and broadband. Return loss of the RF port is better than 10dB. The conversion loss is better than −40 dB, and it is better than −32 dB in 20–40 GHz.

articleTitle: Set Reconciliation for Blockchains with Slepian-Wolf Coding: Deletion Polar Codes
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a polar coding based scheme for set reconciliation between two network nodes. The system is modeled as a well-known Slepian-Wolf setting induced by a fixed number of deletions. The set reconciliation process is divided into two phases: 1) a deletion polar code is employed to help one node to identify the possible deletion indices, which may be larger than the number of genuine deletions; 2) a lossless compression polar code is then designed to feedback those indices with minimum overhead. Our scheme can be viewed as a generalization of polar codes to some emerging network-based applications such as the package synchronization in blockchains. The total overhead is linear to the number of packages, and immune to the package size.

articleTitle: Realize Ultra-Reliability and Low-Latency in Haptic Communication through Prediction
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Haptic communications play an essential role in improving the immersive experience of users. However, it requires a lower latency, as well as the higher continuity and reliability of the received information. Unfortunately, the existing technologies are still not adequate to fully satisfy these requirements, especially when radio resources are limited and the communication environment is fluctuating. To this end, we propose a prediction-based resource allocation scheme for haptic communications to satisfy the low latency and high reliability. Specifically, in order to reduce the risk of latency, we construct a prediction model, which has an optimized prediction window size and uses the LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) method to predict future haptic information. Then, the predicted information would be transmitted in advance according to the window size. In addition, since the prediction model inevitably brings the error, which may well reduce the reliability of haptic transmission. In order to further satisfy reliability and save resources, taking power resources as an example, according to the relationship between power and reliability, we propose optimization problems and solutions based on the relationship between power and reliability. Further, power determines the predicted window size by optimizing the power. Due to optimization problems intractability, we develop a joint bisection and trisection algorithm to obtain the optimal solution. Simulation results show that the optimal transmit power can be obtained, and the error can be minimized through our scheme.

articleTitle: Channel Adaptive Spatial Modulation for Indoor VLC system with Random Direction Mobility
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Multi-input multi-output techniques can obtain a considerable potential in wide bandwidth and high-speed transmission of visible light communication system. In this work, considering the mobility of the user, we propose the adaptive spatial modulation (ASM) scheme and channel adaptive spatial modulation (CASM) scheme to reduce inter-channel interference and improve the bit error rate (BER) performance. In both schemes, the modulation constellation size is adaptively selected based on the distribution of indoor signal-to-noise ratio and optimize the transmit rate while adapting the modulation size to meet the BER requirement. Unlike the ASM scheme, the CASM scheme activates the LED transmitter with best channel gain through feedback. The corresponding closed-form expressions of probability density function and cumulative distribution function are obtained. Numerical results show that the developed ASM frameworks can improve the average spectral efficiency and provide low BER.

articleTitle: The Polarization rotator based on adiabatic waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, an integrated polarization rotator with high efficiency is designed based on twisted waveguide, which can realize the conversion of polarization mode. The polarization rotator is a necessary component in the polarization diversity system, which can suppress the polarization dependent loss, polarization mode dispersion and polarization dependent wavelength caused by birefringence of silicon in the integrated chip. The related data of the designed polarization rotator are simulated and analyzed by full-wave simulation. At the wavelength of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.55\mu m$</tex>, the high cross-polarization conversion efficiency and polarization extinction ratio can be obtained, which are up to 0.996 and 35.03 dB, respectively. The broad working bandwidth of 210 nm is illustrated. Due to its simple structure but high performance, the proposed polarization rotator has promising applications in integrated optics.

articleTitle: Correlated Status Update of Energy Harvesting Sensors Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the development of the Internet of Things, more and more sensors are deployed to monitor the environment status. Due to the limitation on the deployment cost, a large number of sensors need to be deployed wirelessly without stable grid power supply. Therefore, on the one hand, the wireless sensor needs to save energy as much as possible to extend its working time. On the other hand, it needs to sense and transmit timely and accurate information for real-time monitoring. In this paper, we propose a status update control mechanism where an edge node forwards status information from energy-limited energy harvesting sensors to end users based on reinforcement learning. By interacting with the environment, the edge node learns to use the correlation between state updates, which can reduce sensors' energy consumption while ensuring users' quality of service. Simulation results show that compared with several baseline methods, the proposed mechanism can well balance the energy cost and the information error, and significantly reduces the update frequency while ensuring the accuracy of information.

articleTitle: Reliability and Latency of MmWave Communications Based on Blockage Avoidance in Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The millimeter wave(mmWave) communication is a viable approach to support the Gbps data rates that would be required for raw sensor data exchange among autonomous vehicles. However, there is a main challenges resulting from the use of high-frequency bands: the mmWave blockage effect. In this paper, we propose a blockage avoidance based mmWave relay scheme for the Internet of Vehicles. Specifically, we first propose a mmWave link availability identification method based on the vehicle geometric relationship and the spatial correlation between sub-6 GHz signals and mmWave signals. Secondly, in order to improve the reliability of all vehicle sensor data transmission and reduce the overall transmission delay, a resource allocation scheme based on the real-time blocking relationship graph among multilane vehicles is proposed. The simulation show that compared with the baseline, the packet loss rate of proposed scheme is increased by 20%, and the transmission delay is reduced by 80%, which can realize stable, reliable and efficient transmission.

articleTitle: Neural Network Approach to the Estimation of Radiated Emissions from Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Neural Network (NN) and K-means clustering algorithm are used to detect the radiated emission's distribution in printed circuit boards (PCB). The self-organizing map (SOM) network is used for the first layer training. The SOM output data are clustered for the second time by K-means. The elbow method is used as the standard to judge the number of clusters in the final result. The simulation results can show the distribution of PCB radiation sources.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Deployment and Resource Allocation for Energy Efficiency in NOMA Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates the efficient deployment and resource allocation of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to be integrated with wireless terrestrial networks as aerial base stations (BSs) and serve ground user devices by utilizing non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme. Aiming to optimize the energy efficiency (EE) of ground BSs (GBSs) and deployed UAVs, a constrained EE maximization problem is formulated. To solve the optimization problem, we decompose the problem into three subproblems. Firstly, GBS association and subchannel assignment subproblem is formulated and solved by applying matching theory. Then, UAV deployment and subchannel assignment subproblem is formulated. To solve the problem, we propose a clustering strategy based on K-means algorithm to divide users into approximately equal-size clusters. Then, a dynamic many-to-many matching algorithm is proposed to assign subchannels to the users. Finally, a non-convex power allocation subproblem is formulated and solved iteratively using a two-stage quadratic transform. The numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Vector Gaussian Heegard-Berger Problem With Common Reconstructions
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, the vector Gaussian Heegard-Berger problem with common reconstruction constraints is considered. We characterize the rate-distortion function of this instance, when decoders' error covariance distortion constraints are both diagonal positive matrices. In particular, the Timo-Chan-Grant coding scheme is shown to be optimal, via using the source enhancement argument.

articleTitle: Topological multiband photonic chain with one pair of loss and gain defects
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Multiband photonic chains own richer topological properties compared with a lattice of dimers. We investigate one pair of loss and gain defects located on the edges of the topological multiband photonic chain. A photonic chain is composed of unit cells with four elements. In the presence of one pair of loss and gain defects, the chain shows different topological behavior on certain restrictions on intra- and intercell couplings. From the properties of the eigenvalues spectrum, we find that multiple edge states only exist under certain intra- and intercell couplings. We hope our configuration can be useful for topologically protected mode-division multiplexing in photonic devices.

articleTitle: Fast Small Object Detection Algorithm Based on Feature Enhancement and Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Small object detection is one of the research hotspots and challenges in the field of machine vision. Because small targets have fewer pixels in the image, the number of features captured by the first few layers of the target detection network is very small, and the high-level semantic information such as feature classification disappears quickly, making the accuracy of target detection relatively low. The paper uses sub-pixel convolution to reconstruct feature information, uses SE (Squeeze-and-Excitation) attention mechanism to enhance features, and uses U-Net network to capture feature context information and has the advantages of faster detection speed. The algorithm realizes the fast and accurate identification of small targets. Numerical experimental results on the COCO data set and the SUN data set show that the algorithm improved performance by more than 12% in the case of the bounding box AP compared with mainstream algorithms such as YOLOv4.

articleTitle: Denoising Deep Sparse Learning Based Channel Estimation for MU-MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Channel estimation for multi-user multiple input multiple output (MIMO) systems has been recognized as a key issue in next generation wireless communication. The wireless channel is approximately sparse due to the transmission noise effect, which limits the performance of the existing sparse channel estimation method. To address this problem, the denoising deep learning based channel estimation method for MU-MIMO system is proposed in this paper. Utilizing the denoising algorithm to remove noise perturbations in channel estimation, the proposed method can obtain the accurate sparse feature of wireless channels in MU-MIMO system. Moreover, the estimation accuracy and spectrum efficiency can be further improved by fully utilizing the spatial correlation among the massive MIMO channel. Simulation results demonstrated that, the proposed method can improve the channel estimation accuracy and robustness of massive MIMO channel compared with the existing benchmarks.

articleTitle: Edge Computing Empowered Indoor Positioning: A Brief Introduction
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the indoor environment, the accurate of the positioning cannot be guaranteed by the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). Specially, for the power applications, such as large substations and power plant, which have high demand of positioning accuracy, it brings significant challenges. In this paper, we summarize the indoor positioning methods and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each methods. Finally, we focus on the indoor positioning assisted with edge computing. We propose a weighted adaptive KNN algorithm based on the received 5G signal to improve the accuracy of the indoor positioning. Simulations show the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: L1-Norm Distance Metric Learning for Gait Recognition
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Gait recognition is a biometric technology which realizes human identification through the characteristics of human movement during walking. It has a wide range of potential applications in security, surveillance, medical and other fields. In this paper, we propose a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-norm distance Metric Learning (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> ML) method to study the problem of gait recognition. The proposed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> ML aims to learn a linear transformation under large margin framework so that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-norm distance between positive sample pairs in the transformed subspace is smaller than a small threshold, while that of negative sample pairs in the transformed subspace is greater than a large threshold, which can effectively distinguish samples of different subjects. Unlike traditional methods that employ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-norm to calculate the distance between samples, our L1ML utilizes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-norm distance, which is more robust to outlier samples. We conduct a series of comparative experiments on the CASIA-B gait dataset, and the experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Estimate the Coordinates of LEDs in Wireless Optical Positioning Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Traditional visible light positioning (VLP) systems estimate receivers' coordinates based on the known light-emitting diode (LED) coordinates. However, the LED coordinates are not always known accurately. Because of the structural changes of the buildings due to temperature, humidity or material aging, even measured by highly accurate laser range finders, the LED coordinates may change unpredictably. In this paper, we propose an easy and low-cost method to update the position information of the LEDs. We use two optical angle-of-arrival (AOA) estimators to detect the beam directions of the LEDs. Each AOA estimator has four differently oriented photodiodes (PDs). Considering the additive noises of the PDs, we derive the closed-form error expression for the proposed LED coordinates estimator. Both analytical and Monte Carlo experimental results show that the layout of the AOA estimators could affect the estimation error. These results may provide intuitive insights for the design of the optical indoor positioning systems.

articleTitle: A Mobility Aware Task Offloading Scheme For Vehicle Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The mobility of the vehicle poses new challenges to the unloading decision. In view of this situation, this paper proposes a unloading scheme of vehicle edge computing (VEC) based on mobile sensing, so that vehicles with computing ability can provide VEC services in the vehicle fog network, so as to solve the problem of high-speed mobility of vehicles. Firstly, we divide the running time of each vehicle into several same time slots. In each time slot, we believe that the distance between the vehicle and the base station is constant. RSU distributes a task to multiple vehicles according to the ratio, and optimizes the energy consumption of the system by optimizing the task unloading ratio. Then a Lagrange and its dual method based on convex algorithm is used to solve this problem, and a low complexity algorithm is proposed to optimize the task unloading ratio, and the Lagrange multiplier is iterative until it converges. Finally, the simulation results verify the efficient performance of the proposed scheme. Compared with other algorithms, the proposed algorithm not only improves the utilization rate of vehicle computing resources, but also minimizes the overall energy consumption of the system.

articleTitle: Flicker-Free Adaptive Enhancement for Infrared Video
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Infrared videos often suffer from low contrast and insufficient texture. In order to improve poor visual effect, a novel infrared video enhancement method is proposed, which contains intra-frame brightness enhancement and inter-frame brightness continuity adjustment. In intra-frame brightness enhancement, it has two steps including global contrast enhancement and local details enhancement. To global contrast enhancement, the processed image contrast by geometric distribution, and it is incorporated into an optimization problem with a sorted histogram of each frame to yield a modified histogram. To local details enhancement, after Retinex decomposition, the reflection component is magnified by boundary preserving filter, and this strategy can effectively suppress noise in relatively uniform regions. Furthermore, to maintain inter-frame brightness continuity, adaptive parameters are introduced through optical flow to control the combination ratio of geometric distribution histogram, in which the enhancement degree of each frame can be adjusted according to inter-frame similarity and the moving region are enhanced adaptively according to the change of each frame. Experimental results demonstrate that proposed algorithm can effectively enhance the contrast and detail of infrared video, and improve the visual effect in subjective and objective quality evaluation.

articleTitle: Location Aware Multi-cell MIMO Communications Assisted by Optical Positioning
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-energy-efficiency location aware multi-cell multiple input multiple output (MIMO) communication system assisted by optical positioning. The location information acquisition method in the optical positioning subsystem has been designed, which can perform real-time angle of arrival and distance estimation for users and other scatterers and identify the users through the feedback signal.
